specific_source.citation: Lehtonen (2008), An integrative approach to species delimitation in Echinodorus, Kew Bulletin 63: 525–563
specific_source.view: Kew POWO general information reproduces source attribution under synonym Echinodorus cordifolius

source_reported_morphology.habit: Perennial, rhizomatous aquatic or wetland herb, to about 200 cm
source_reported_morphology.leaves: Emergent ovate to oval leaf blades 7–30 × 4–20 cm, about 5–9 major veins, leaf base attenuate to cordate, petioles 11–60 cm
source_reported_morphology.inflorescence: Racemose to paniculate, 3–8 whorls of 6–22 flowers, decumbent and potentially producing vegetative plantlets
source_reported_morphology.flower: White petals; flowers 2–3.5 cm across; 15–28 stamens
source_reported_morphology.achene: 1.3–3 mm long, ribbed and keeled, with circular glands separated by ribs and a terminal erect beak

key_literature_comparison: Flora of North America formerly treats this as Echinodorus cordifolius, with a subspecies concept; do not copy subspecies-only details onto all modern Aquarius specimens.
source_anomaly: Kew display of the quoted 2008 description contains an implausible petal dimension (13 cm); this value is explicitly excluded pending inspection of original article. Other listed flower dimensions are cross-check targets, not substitute correction of the apparent typo.
preservation: Additive research only; images/photo rights/public site unchanged
